body:
Hi,

I just got this issue while adding shader debug info generation into our game:

```
dxc -T ps_6_0 /Zi -Fd "d:\debug_info_folder\" mySimplePS.hlsl
```
dxc failed : Required input file argument is missing. use -help to get more information.

This issue can be worked around by :
- removing the double quote (but that's not always possible),
- replacing anti slashes by slashes (but has issue for include paths with -I),
- removing trailing anti slash (may not be desired with -Fd)

Not sure if this issue is related to https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2319#issue-465526382

Cheers,
Olivier

comments.body:
The final backslash in ``"d:\debug_info_folder\"`` is causing the close quote to be escaped. As a result, the parameter to ``-Fd`` is taken as the complete rest of the line without a terminating quotation mark. It may seem odd from this use case, but it is needed to handle file names with a quotation mark in them (which, granted, is also pretty odd). Nevertheless, I think this would be considered correct behavior for the command line you've given. Can the final ``\`` be removed? Can it be replaced by ``"d:\debug_info_folder\\"``? Either of these should resolve the issue. 

Edit: wow. even convincing this hypertext to print two backslashes in a row is tricky.

I've just tested with fxc (on -I option) and it has the same issue indeed. 
The thing is the trailing double quote is needed when we want to let dxc chose the debug info file name:
```
-Fd <file>              Write debug information to the given file, or automatically named file in directory when ending in '\'
```

I see the problem now. I wasn't aware of that aspect of this parameter. 

I agree something needs to be fixed so that quoted directory names can be provided. I'll poke at this some today unless someone more influential wants to swoop in and weigh in and/or solve the problem.

I'm afraid the problem, such as it is, extends beyond the confines of this project. I knew that Linux accounted for escaped characters in its division of main function argv parameters, so I dusted off my Windows build and tried it there where I found the same behavior. As a result, the given command line results in just 6 args by combining the last two as one.

DXC could fix the problem by reparsing the arguments. In fact, LLVM has code to do just that used by other binaries, but not dxc. I wonder if, perhaps, the better solution is to change the way a directory is indicated. Perhaps via a separate flag. Maybe adding a separate flag as an option to get around this sort of problem might maintain backward compatibility while fixing this conundrum. 

I did come up with a workaround that might be acceptable. If you transpose the quotation mark and the backslash, the quotation mark is no longer escaped and the parameter ends with a backslash but any components of the full path that might require quoting are still quoted. So that . . . 

    dxc -T ps_6_0 /Zi -Fd "d:\debug_info_folder\" mySimplePS.hlsl

becomes

    dxc -T ps_6_0 /Zi -Fd "d:\debug_info_folder"\ mySimplePS.hlsl

Hope that helps.  WIthout further guidance from someone empowered to make decisions about this project, I don't feel I can contribute any further.
And then I indulged in googling you and discover you're working on Beyond Good and Evil 2?!? 😲 I loved the original!

Indeed I'm working on that game :).

I was wondering myself if we could have a separate option to specify debug folder, not file, for which the final antislash wouldn't be required, since it's a folder. For example:
```
-Fdd "d:\debug_info_folder"
```
That's exactly the flag name I was thinking of. It's simple enough. I can code it up and we'll see what the powers that be say.
Marked this as dormat - it looks like there may be a PR that addresses this still open and we'll accept that if someone wants to rebase it and  finish it off.

title: Compiler fails on quoted folder parameters finishing with '\\'
